annotations.description: Casting Ponder before playing a land is a sequencing error. GPT4om Valley has multiple fetchlands and lands in hand but cast Ponder first. If Ponder reveals good cards and they choose not to shuffle, they lose no value. But if they want to shuffle (which is common with Ponder), they should play a fetchland first so they have the option to fetch after seeing the top 3 but before drawing. More importantly, playing a land first preserves mana flexibility - they could play a fetchland, cast Ponder, then crack the fetch if they don't like what they see. Additionally, if Ponder reveals they want to play Phelia this turn, they need to have already played their land to have WU available. By casting Ponder before land drop, they're using their only blue mana and can't cast anything else this turn regardless of what Ponder shows (unless they find and play an untapped blue source).

annotations.description: Playing Ancient Tomb sacrifices City of Traitors (which produces CC without life cost). More importantly, the player could have played Wasteland instead (to destroy one of the opponent's key lands like Karakas or a dual land) or Abundant Countryside without losing City of Traitors' free mana. The player had Wasteland in hand which could have been played as a land drop to threaten the opponent's mana base while keeping City of Traitors. Playing Ancient Tomb here is a net downgrade - losing City of Traitors (free CC) and replacing it with Ancient Tomb (CC with 2 damage). Wasteland would have been strictly better as the land drop since it preserves City of Traitors and provides utility to destroy opponent's nonbasic lands.

annotations.description: Casting Brainstorm during their own main phase instead of holding it for the opponent's end step or in response to something. Brainstorm is almost always better cast at instant speed at end of turn to maximize information and keep mana open. Additionally, with Wasteland available, they should consider using Wasteland to destroy one of the opponent's key lands (Eye of Ugin, Eldrazi Temple, Ancient Tomb, or Cavern of Souls) before the opponent untaps and can use them. The opponent at 30 life with Eldrazi threats is the bigger concern, and destroying Eye of Ugin or Eldrazi Temple would significantly hamper their mana development. Brainstorm without a shuffle effect available (no fetchlands on board) is also less valuable - they're just putting two cards back on top with no way to shuffle them away.

annotations.betterLine: Activate Wasteland to destroy Eye of Ugin (or Eldrazi Temple) to cut off the opponent's cost reduction/mana advantage, then hold Brainstorm for the opponent's end step or a future turn when a fetchland is available to shuffle away unwanted cards.

annotations.description: Sonnet Gramps declined to untap Grim Monolith at the end of the opponent's turn when they had 6 mana available (Ancient Tomb for 2, Eldrazi Temple for 1-2, Cavern of Souls for 1, Eye of Ugin for 0). With Ancient Tomb (2) + Eldrazi Temple (1 or 2) + Cavern of Souls (1) = 4-5 mana, they couldn't pay the 4 to untap Grim Monolith this turn. Actually, let me recalculate: Ancient Tomb produces 2, Eldrazi Temple produces 1 (or 2 for Eldrazi), Cavern of Souls produces 1, Eye of Ugin produces 0 mana. That's 4 mana available (or 5 if spending on Eldrazi). They could pay exactly 4 to untap Grim Monolith at end of opponent's turn, which would give them access to 3 additional colorless mana on their own turn. This would enable casting Eldrazi Linebreaker (1CR) and potentially Kozilek's Command with a larger X value. Missing this is a minor inefficiency.

annotations.betterLine: Tap Ancient Tomb (2 colorless, take 2 damage) + Eldrazi Temple (1 colorless) + Cavern of Souls (1 colorless) to pay 4 and untap Grim Monolith, giving access to 3 extra mana on their next turn for bigger plays like Kozilek's Command or deploying multiple threats.

annotations.description: GPT4om Valley chose to exile Grim Monolith with Leyline Binding instead of Wastescape Battlemage. Wastescape Battlemage is a 2/2 creature that can attack and deal damage, while Grim Monolith is a mana rock that's currently untapped but the opponent already has significant mana on board (Eldrazi Temple, Cavern of Souls, Eye of Ugin, Ancient Tomb, Wasteland, plus the Monolith). However, Grim Monolith produces 3 colorless mana which enables casting expensive Eldrazi threats faster. The opponent is at 28 life and GPT4om Valley is at 13 with an empty hand - they're in a losing position where the opponent casting another large Eldrazi could be game-ending. Exiling Grim Monolith slows down the opponent's mana development, but the Battlemage is already on board as a threat and could be relevant if the opponent has ways to re-kick it or if it represents immediate board pressure. Given the opponent still has Eye of Ugin, Eldrazi Temple, Ancient Tomb, Cavern of Souls, and Wasteland, removing Grim Monolith reduces their mana from roughly 9+ to 6, which could matter for casting 7+ cost Eldrazi. This is a close call - Grim Monolith is arguably the right target since it represents the most mana acceleration, but the Battlemage could also be important as it can attack and the opponent could use it to bounce or exile GPT4om Valley's permanents if they replay it with kicker.
annotations.actionTaken: Exiled Grim Monolith with Leyline Binding
annotations.betterLine: This is debatable - exiling Wastescape Battlemage removes an immediate creature threat and prevents potential kicker value if it gets blinked or recurred, while exiling Grim Monolith cuts mana production. Given the opponent already has substantial mana sources and the Battlemage is tapped (already attacked), Grim Monolith may be the correct choice to prevent casting massive Eldrazi like Sire of Seven Deaths. The play is defensible.

annotations.betterLine: Cast Reality Smasher (cost reduced to {2}{C} by Eye of Ugin) using Ancient Tomb + Eldrazi Temple, then attack with both Reality Smasher (5/5 haste trample) and Wastescape Battlemage for 7 total damage.
